title: klix glossary document
description: A klix glossary: concepts mapped to per-language term lists. This document format is stable and hand-writable — you do not need klix's build pipeline to author one. Both the versioned document (with schema_version/concepts) and the bare concept map are accepted by klix; the versioned form is preferred for anything you intend to distribute, because it carries provenance.

bare_map.title: Bare concept map (legacy)
bare_map.description: The original shape: every top-level key is a concept. No version, no provenance. Still accepted; use the versioned document for anything shared.

propertyNames.description: Document-level keys are not concept names — their presence would make this a versioned document, so the two branches stay disjoint.

schema_version.description: Format version. klix refuses a document whose version is NEWER than the build understands, instead of parsing it optimistically. Current version: 1.

concepts.description: The vocabulary. Concept key -> per-language terms.

description.description: Optional human-readable summary of what this glossary covers.

source.description: Where this glossary came from. PROVENANCE IS PER GLOSSARY, never per concept — one record covers the whole file, so it stays a single entry no matter how many concepts the glossary holds.

license.description: Licence of THIS glossary. Must be compatible with the project you bundle it into — a share-alike or copyleft source cannot be merged into an MIT package. Recorded verbatim; klix does not interpret it.

glossary_source.description: Alternative spelling of `source`, accepted so a machine-generated header can group the two provenance fields together.

concept.title: One concept and its terms
concept.description: A language map plus optional metadata tags. Every key other than `tags` is an ISO-639-1 language code; any number of languages is allowed and there is no fixed pair — a concept may have one language or ten.

additionalProperties.description: A term list, or the reserved `tags` list. anyOf rather than oneOf: both are lists of strings and the loader separates them by key name, so requiring exactly one match would make every valid document fail.

items.description: One term. No duplicates within a concept — a term maps to exactly one concept across the WHOLE glossary (klix's index is flat), so the same word under two concepts is refused, not merged.

tags.title: Free metadata tags
tags.description: Optional, free-form labels such as ['manufacturing'] or ['workplace','hr']. Tags are METADATA ONLY: they do not take part in validation and there is no 'domain' concept in the engine. They exist so a caller can filter (e.g. 'give me every concept tagged it') without that filtering affecting merge or conflict rules.
